new_sources.summary: This article explores the history of the Billings Method, a form of 'natural' family planning, in Ireland from its initial popularisation in the 1970s to the beginning of its decline in the late 1980s. Drawing on oral history interviews with women who taught the method in Ireland in this period, as well as previously unexplored archival sources, the article seeks to nuance understandings of conservative women's activism in this period. It argues that the Billings movement had much in common with the tenets of feminist health activism. However, promoters of the method ultimately failed to garner support from members of the Irish medical profession and Catholic Church hierarchy.
new_sources.title: The Billings Ovulation Method and Catholic Women's Health Activism in 1970s and 1980s Ireland.

new_sources.title: Transnational voting as collective action in liminal occasion: Examination of political mobilization of non-resident Turkish citizens in Germany.
